name: Atyap
description: The Atyap (Kataf) people are one of Southern Kaduna’s largest communities, known for rich yam festivals, traditional weaving, and layered hill settlements.
highlights: Home of the annual harvest festival
Strong cultural identity in Zangon Kataf
seeMore: The Atyap celebrate the end of planting season with vibrant dance and masked performances.
Their clan system supports inter-communal trade and historic market traditions.

name: Bajju
description: Bajju is famed for fertile farming valleys, yam cultivation, and strong hillside homesteads around Kachia.
seeMore: Bajju women are celebrated for colorful cloth and beadwork.
Markets in Kachia draw traders from across the region.

name: Ham
description: The Ham people conserve an old palace culture and host one of the region’s most distinctive festivals in Jaba.
seeMore: Ham hilltops have scenic views over the plateau.
The Zhuing festival features masquerades and communal feasts.

name: Irri gwe
description: Irigwe communities live on the plateau edge and combine cattle rearing with cassava and yam farms.
seeMore: Irigwe music uses drum ensembles and flute melodies.
Traditional dances mark harvest and marriage seasons.

name: Gwong
description: Gwong are centered around Kagoro, with palaces, lively markets, and a strong reputation for preserved oral history.
seeMore: Gwong storytellers pass legends through generations.
Visitors find colorful cloth and dried yam in local markets.

name: Adara
description: Adara communities are known for rich hill forests, fishing ponds, and a strong yam festival tradition.
seeMore: Adara women make colorful woven bags and baskets.
Folklore connects natural springs with ancestral spirits.

name: Kagoro (Agworok)
description: Kagoro is an important cultural center famous for music, hillside views, and warm community hospitality.
seeMore: Kagoro elders recount migration stories at communal fires.
The town hosts regional tourism during festival weeks.

name: Ninzam
description: The Ninzam people keep a close-knit agricultural community with a strong language identity.
highlights: High percentage of native language speakers
seeMore: Ninzam cuisine includes unique soups and vegetable dishes.
Young people often study in nearby towns while preserving language skills.

name: Numana
description: Numana is a small highland community with rich agricultural traditions and heritage celebrations.
seeMore: Numana folk songs honor ancestors and the land.
Elders carefully preserve traditional medicinal knowledge.

name: Nandu
description: Nandu is known for vibrant harvest celebrations and busy local trading centers.
seeMore: Nandu dancers wear carved wooden masks.
Local cuisine highlights roasted yams and millets.

name: Ninzom
description: Ninzom communities are recognized for their unique crafts and a commitment to preserving native language use.
seeMore: Many Ninzom speakers use oral history to teach youth.
Their pottery and woven goods are prized in local markets.

name: Sholio
description: Sholio people live in hillside settlements and mark the season with music and harvest rites.
seeMore: Sholio children learn song and dance from elders.
Their festival is a major draw for neighboring villages.

name: Ikulu
description: Ikulu people maintain agricultural homes and a language with strong ancestral song traditions.
seeMore: Ikulu artisans make colorful leather goods.
Their harvest feast invites neighboring clans to share food.

name: Akurmi
description: Akurmi villages are known for grain production and traditional festivities centering on song and dance.
seeMore: Akurmi artisans weave mats for market sales.
Young dancers train for community ceremonies.

name: Moroa
description: Moroa is a farming community with communal markets and historic settlement patterns.
seeMore: Moroa elders counsel youth on land stewardship.
Their festival features native flute music.

name: Atsam
description: Atsam communities are tightly woven around harvest celebrations and ancestral village rituals.
seeMore: Atsam children play traditional musical games.
Families gather for multi-course harvest meals.

name: Aminu
description: Aminu is a trading community known for maize farms and welcoming markets.
seeMore: Aminu traders travel to nearby towns for seasonal trade.
The festival brings visitors from neighboring communities.

name: Zari
description: Zari families balance livestock rearing with small-scale farming and heritage celebrations.
seeMore: Zari herders move cattle during seasonal rains.
Local women make woven containers from grass.

name: Tum
description: Tum people farm yams and cassava while preserving community heritage through storytelling.
seeMore: Tum elders host youth councils during harvest.
Their songs often describe the natural landscape.

name: Zangon
description: Zangon is a historic market hub and cultural center with strong language and tradition preservation.
seeMore: Zangon leaders maintain community archives.
Market days often double as festival occasions.
